pages.text: "Look! Waves as big as mountains!" Dari pressed his nose to the top room's glass. The lighthouse beam turned around them. Sky dark, sea churning—"I'll wait for an even bigger wave!"
Wind slammed the glass. Windows rattled, rain tapped, and an iron ring jingled beside the lamp. Dari flinched but stayed. "Stronger!"
Dad climbed up quickly. "Not beside the windows in strong wind, Dari. The light turns by itself. Let's go down." His voice was steady. Dari stepped away and held his flipper. "Okay."
They went down the spiral stairs step by step. At the bottom, Mom waited with a quilt beside the stove. All three settled together, cozy as a burrow.

Dad whispered, "Let's be sea snails. In wind, they hide deep in their shells. The lighthouse is our shell. This is its deepest part." Dari pulled the quilt over his head. Wind howled, but here was warm.
Dad taught three promises. "One, strong wind—downstairs, not the top room! Two, away from glass, beside the stove! Three, go up with a grown-up once it stops!" Dari nodded. "Like a sea snail!"
Dari curled between Mom and Dad and waited. Outside, bangs and howls; inside, the stove crackled warmly. "Strong wind? Go downstairs!" he repeated softly.
The wind stopped. Holding Dari's flipper, Dad went upstairs. Beyond the windows, the sea was calm; the lamp still turned. Dari slapped his tail. "I didn't cry at all!"
Now Dari knew the promises. "One, wind means downstairs! Two, away from glass! Three, upstairs with a grown-up when it stops!" Folding the quilt, he called the words loudly.
Dad lifted him. "Scary wind, but you kept every promise!" Going downstairs beside the stove had kept them snug through the wind. "Strong wind? Go downstairs!" Dari smiled in his arms.
